Valid and Peek: A Parent’s Guide to Evaluating Compliment Apps

By the Valid team · Published September 13, 2026

Valid — Compliment Classmates and Peek: Secret Compliment are separate, unaffiliated apps. If a headline, school notice, or social post discusses a compliment app, check the exact app name before applying its claims to another product. Similar invitation wording does not establish that two apps have the same features or policies.

Which app do the cited warnings concern?

The KNWA/FOX24 report identifies Peek: Secret Compliment and quotes concerns from Rogers Public Schools. Officer Gomez’s warning post also names Peek. Those specific warnings concern Peek; they do not establish that Valid uses the contact-list messaging behavior they describe.

Installing Valid or granting contact access does not automatically send invitations to everyone in your phone book using your number. Members choose whether to send invitations through their phone’s message composer. For activity notifications sent through Valid’s messaging service, our policy is to send with recipient consent and honor opt-outs.

Start with the product you are actually reviewing

Check the app’s full name, store listing, and official support website. For Valid, our official website is validapp.lol, and our iPhone App Store listing identifies Valid — Compliment Classmates. Our parent FAQ explains our own practices.

This guide is written by the Valid team. It describes Valid’s published policies and offers questions families can ask about any compliment app. It is not an independent safety rating or a verified feature audit of Peek.

Compare specific safeguards

Ask whether polls are reviewed before publication, what behavior is prohibited, and how a student can get help. Valid’s published policy is human review of every poll before publication. Our rules prohibit bullying, harassment, impersonation, and vote manipulation, and students have reporting and blocking tools.

Also ask what a response-time promise covers. Valid publishes an under-15-minute moderation SLA as a service commitment. That commitment does not guarantee that every interaction is harmless or that every concern is fully resolved in 15 minutes.

Look closely at anonymity and purchases

“Anonymous” can describe different experiences. On Valid, voter identities are hidden by default, but reveal features can show the voter’s name and profile photo to the recipient. Valid offers optional purchases, including God Mode with reveal benefits. Families should review the in-app price and benefits before buying.

When evaluating another app, check its current explanation of what can be revealed, who can see it, and which features cost money. Do not assume that the same word on two store listings means the same privacy protection.

Ask how contacts and invitations work

Valid uses contacts to help connect people who know each other. Contacts can be included in polls before they register. Texts can be member-shared invitations or activity notifications sent by Valid. Our text-message guide explains the distinction and how to request that texts stop, information be removed, and a number be excluded from voting.

For any app, look for direct answers about people who have not joined and whether they can ask for help without installing it. Compare what the policy actually says, rather than relying only on a positive slogan or a critical headline.

Choose based on your student’s experience

We built Valid to help classmates express appreciation and connect. Families can evaluate that aim alongside our specific tools, disclosures, and their student’s experience. We do not have independent comparative evidence establishing that Valid is safer than Peek. A useful decision considers the current policies of each app and whether participating feels comfortable for the student.
